items.topic: Disulfiram — avoid alcohol and alcohol-containing products; reaction risk persists after last dose
items.stem: A client starting disulfiram for alcohol use disorder asks what to avoid. Which teaching is most accurate?

options.text: Avoid alcoholic beverages and alcohol-containing products (e.g., some cough syrups/elixirs); unpleasant reactions can still occur for days after the last dose
Alcohol is safe with disulfiram if limited to one beer with meals
Only distilled spirits interact; wine and beer never cause a reaction
Disulfiram may be started while the client is currently intoxicated to ‘reset’ tolerance

rationales.A: Correct. Merck: drinking within 12 hours of disulfiram causes flushing/tachycardia/sweating and possibly hypotension; medications containing alcohol (tinctures, elixirs, some OTC cough/cold preparations) must also be avoided; effects may persist days after the last dose. OpenStax: abstain ≥12 hours before starting; reactions can occur up to 2 weeks after discontinuation; avoid nontraditional alcohol sources (mouthwash, cough syrup, hand sanitizer).
rationales.B: Incorrect. Even small amounts of alcohol can trigger a reaction.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Any alcohol source can trigger the reaction.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Disulfiram must not be given during intoxication; wait ≥12 hours after drinking.

sources.title: Alcohol Use Disorder and Rehabilitation
sources.evidence: Drinking within 12 hours causes facial flushing, tachycardia, sweating; high alcohol doses may cause nausea/hypotension; medications containing alcohol (tinctures, elixirs, some OTC cough/cold preparations) must be avoided; effects may persist 3–7 days after last dose.

sources.title: 15.3 Alcohol Use Disorder Drugs
sources.evidence: Abstain from alcohol ≥12 hours before starting; reactions can occur up to 2 weeks after discontinuation; avoid mouthwashes, cough syrups, hand sanitizers, and other alcohol-containing products; never administer while intoxicated.

items.topic: Metronidazole — avoid alcohol during therapy and for 3 days after last dose (disulfiram-like reaction)
items.stem: A client prescribed oral metronidazole asks about drinking alcohol. Which instruction is correct?

options.text: Avoid alcohol while taking metronidazole and for at least 3 days after the final dose to reduce risk of a disulfiram-like reaction (flushing, headache, nausea/vomiting)
Alcohol is encouraged because it improves metronidazole absorption
Only red wine interacts; clear liquors are always safe
Alcohol may be resumed the same evening as the last dose

rationales.A: Correct. Merck: a disulfiram-like reaction may occur if alcohol is ingested within 3 days of use. MedlinePlus: do not drink alcoholic beverages or take products with alcohol/propylene glycol while taking metronidazole and for at least 3 days after the final dose.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Alcohol can cause an unpleasant reaction, not improved absorption.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Any alcohol may trigger the reaction.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Continue avoidance for at least 3 days after the last dose.

sources.title: Metronidazole and Tinidazole
sources.evidence: Disulfiram-like reaction (flushing, headache, nausea, vomiting) may occur if alcohol is ingested within 3 days of use.

sources.title: Metronidazole
sources.evidence: Do not drink alcoholic beverages or take products with alcohol or propylene glycol while taking this medication and for at least 3 days after your final dose; may cause nausea, vomiting, cramps, headache, sweating, flushing.

items.topic: Alendronate — take with plain water on empty stomach; remain upright ≥30 minutes
items.stem: Which teaching is essential for a client starting oral alendronate for osteoporosis?

options.text: Take with a full glass of plain water on an empty stomach in the morning, and remain sitting or standing upright for at least 30 minutes before lying down or taking other food/medications
Take with milk at bedtime and lie flat immediately to improve absorption
Crush the tablet into orange juice and take with breakfast
Take only with coffee to enhance bone uptake

rationales.A: Correct. OpenStax: take with 6–8 oz water and sit/stand ≥30 minutes to prevent esophageal irritation. MedlinePlus: morning empty stomach; do not lie down for ≥30 minutes; swallow tablet with plain water only (not tea/coffee/juice/milk).
rationales.B: Incorrect. Bedtime/lying flat and milk increase esophageal risk and impair absorption.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Do not crush into juice; take whole with plain water before food.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Coffee is not an appropriate liquid vehicle.

sources.title: 27.3 Calcium Preparations, Vitamin D, Bisphosphonates, Calcimimetics, and Peptide Hormones
sources.evidence: Take with 6–8 ounces of water; sit/stand for at least 30 minutes after administration to prevent esophageal irritation; contraindicated if unable to stand/sit upright for 30 minutes.

sources.title: Alendronate
sources.section: How should this medicine be used? — upright 30 minutes
sources.evidence: Take just after getting out of bed, before food/drink; do not lie down ≥30 minutes; sit/stand upright until ≥30 minutes have passed and first food eaten; swallow tablet with full glass of plain water only.

items.topic: Phantom limb pain — acknowledge that the pain is real; do not dismiss the sensation
items.stem: After a below-knee amputation, a client reports burning pain in the missing foot. Which nursing response is most appropriate?

options.text: Acknowledge that phantom limb pain is a real neuropathic sensation after amputation and assess/manage the pain
Tell the client the pain is imaginary because the foot is gone
Ignore the report because phantom sensations never require treatment
Immediately remove the residual-limb dressing and discard all analgesics as unnecessary

rationales.A: Correct. OpenStax: phantom pain is caused by misinterpreted signals, but the pain is real. Merck lists phantom limb pain as a neuropathic/deafferentation pain syndrome felt in the region of an amputated body part.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Dismissing the pain as imaginary is inaccurate and nontherapeutic.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Phantom pain often requires assessment and management.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Do not discard needed dressings/analgesics based on misunderstanding of phantom pain.

sources.title: 7.1 Concepts and Causes of Pain
sources.evidence: After amputation, phantom pain is perceived from the missing body part; brain misinterprets signals, but the pain is real; rule out other causes such as infection.

sources.title: Neuropathic Pain
sources.evidence: Phantom limb pain is listed among postsurgical neuropathic syndromes; deafferentation pain felt in the region of an amputated body part.

items.topic: Chest tube water-seal chamber — continuous bubbling suggests air leak; check connections and notify
items.stem: While assessing a closed chest-tube drainage system, the nurse notes continuous bubbling in the water-seal chamber. What is the priority interpretation and action?

options.text: Continuous bubbling may indicate an air leak; check the drain/tubing for disconnection, dislodgement, or loose connections, assess the client, and notify the provider if the problem cannot be corrected
Continuous bubbling always means the system is perfectly sealed and needs no further assessment
Ignore bubbling and clamp the chest tube tightly for the remainder of the shift without assessment
Pour oil into the water-seal chamber to stop all bubbling permanently

rationales.A: Correct. Open RN: continuous bubbling in the water-seal chamber may indicate an air leak; check connections/site and notify if uncorrected. RCH: continuous bubbling indicates a large air leak between drain and patient—check disconnection/dislodgement/loose connection, assess, and notify medical staff if not remedied.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Continuous bubbling is a cue for possible air leak, not assurance of a perfect seal.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Indiscriminate prolonged clamping without troubleshooting is unsafe.

sources.evidence: Tidaling indicates patency; continuous bubbling in the water seal chamber may indicate an air leak; identify/correct external leaks such as loose connections; notify provider if leak cannot be corrected.

sources.evidence: Continuous bubbling indicates large air leak between the drain and the patient; check disconnection, dislodgement, loose connection; assess patient; notify medical staff immediately if problem cannot be remedied.

items.topic: Newborn ocular prophylaxis — erythromycin 0.5% ointment both eyes soon after birth
items.stem: Which action correctly provides prophylaxis against gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum for a healthy term newborn?

options.text: Instill erythromycin 0.5% ophthalmic ointment into both eyes as soon as possible after birth (ideally soon after delivery; ensure within 24 hours if delayed)
Wait until the 2-week well-baby visit to apply any eye ointment
Apply antibiotic ointment to only one eye to ‘test tolerance’
Flush both eyes with undiluted household bleach instead of ointment

rationales.A: Correct. CDC: erythromycin 0.5% ointment in each eye in a single application at birth, as soon as possible after delivery (vaginal or cesarean), with a system to ensure prophylaxis <24 hours if delayed. Merck: topical antimicrobial ointment to both eyes; erythromycin 0.5% recommended in the United States.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Prophylaxis is given soon after birth, not delayed weeks.

sources.title: Gonococcal Infections Among Neonates — STI Treatment Guidelines
sources.publisher: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
sources.evidence: Erythromycin 0.5% ophthalmic ointment in each eye in a single application at birth; instill into both eyes as soon as possible after delivery; ensure <24 hours if delayed.

sources.title: Initial Evaluation and Preventive Care in the Healthy Term Newborn
sources.evidence: Topical antimicrobial ointment to both eyes to prevent gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum; erythromycin 0.5% ointment recommended in the United States.

items.topic: Ontario — practising nursing while impaired by any substance is professional misconduct
items.stem: An Ontario nurse realizes that a recently used substance may be impairing judgment before a scheduled shift. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Practising nursing while impaired by any substance is professional misconduct; the nurse must not practise while impaired and should seek help if health affects safe practice
Working impaired is acceptable if the nurse ‘feels fine enough’ to finish charting only
Only illegal substances count; prescribed medications never impair practice
Impairment is solely an employer HR issue and is never a professional-misconduct concern in Ontario

rationales.A: Correct. O. Reg. 799/93 lists practising while the member’s ability is impaired by any substance as professional misconduct. CNO Code of Conduct 6.8: nurses do not practise when impaired by any substance; 6.7: seek help if health affects safe practice.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Impairment precludes safe practice regardless of limited tasks.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Any impairing substance is within the regulation’s scope.
rationales.D: Incorrect. It is defined professional misconduct under Ontario regulation and CNO standards.

sources.title: O. Reg. 799/93 Professional Misconduct
sources.evidence: Practising the profession while the member’s ability to do so is impaired by any substance is professional misconduct.

sources.title: Code of Conduct
sources.evidence: 6.7 Nurses self-reflect on health and seek help if their health affects their ability to practice safely. 6.8 Nurses do not practice when impaired by any substance.
